By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:25.

Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin in the final round of the Nations League group stage.

In a convincing performance, the four-time world champions produced their best football since the arrival of Jurgen Klopp, who took charge of the national team after the disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

With goals from Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, Brajan Gruda and Florian Wirtz, who scored twice, the Germans produced an impressive result against opponents who were also fighting for top spot in the group.

The victory took on even greater importance because of the situation before the match. Germany began the round in third place in Group A2, level on points with Greece and behind the Dutch, and risked missing out on the quarter-finals. With the win, they reached 11 points, overtook their rivals on goal difference and finished the first phase at the top, securing a place among the best eight in the competition.

Recent findings suggest that one of the stars of the night was Derry Scherhant. Klopp’s selection on the left of the attack scored his first goal for the senior Germany team.

A native of Berlin, the 24-year-old winger, who plays for Freiburg, took the opportunity to make his mark in front of the crowd of his home city. His exuberant celebration after finding the top corner past Bart Verbruggen reflected the special significance of the moment in his international career.

Industry observers note that the goal also rewarded the faith the manager has placed in the attacker. Scherhant was only making his fourth appearance for the national team and has earned his place amid the renewal carried out by Klopp since he took over.

The chance given to the Freiburg player is part of a strategy that seeks to widen the squad’s options, without restricting selections to the best-known names in German football. Against the Netherlands, the youngster delivered and highlighted that he can be an interesting option in attack.

It has been revealed that another standout was Wirtz, who again showed how his talent can make a difference in a Germany shirt. The attacking midfielder scored twice in the second half and was decisive in turning a lead built before the break into a rout. His ability to find space, accelerate attacks and arrive in positions to shoot gave another dimension to the German attack.

The performance reinforces one of the main positive certainties of the early days of Klopp’s reign: Wirtz is capable of taking on the team’s technical leadership.

As well as the brilliance of the number 17 and Scherhant’s first goal, the match also underlined the importance of the opportunities given to other young players. Gruda, who had already scored in the 3-1 win over Serbia, found the net again during this international break and has now scored two goals for the national team.

Recent findings suggest that left-back Philipp Treu was also among the starters, benefiting from the opening up of opportunities by the manager. These are names that help to give shape to a project still under construction and show that Klopp intends to increase competition in different positions.

In a recent development, it was a well-played and competitive first half, with good link-up play and quick transitions. At home, Germany had more possession and went for a proactive game, with a high line and patience to find space.

In the 41st minute, they found it: Scherhant received the ball on the right, got past Denzel Dumfries and curled a lovely shot across goal into the top corner past Verbruggen.

It has been revealed that the Netherlands, for their part, took to the pitch practically already qualified. In their tactical approach in the first half, the Dutch opted for a more reactive game: either Xavi Hernandez’s team reached dangerous areas through counter-attacks, or they drew in the German press and built from the back, passing the ball patiently.

In a recent development, at the start of the second half, Germany needed only a few minutes to punish the visitors again. Fourteen minutes into the half, Wirtz began a move down the left, tried to play a one-two with Scherhant, but saw Dumfries step in front of him. The Liverpool midfielder then regained the ball, dribbled past the Dutch full-back and struck hard with his left foot from the edge of the area to make it 2-0.

Industry observers note that from there it became a stroll. The Netherlands clearly felt the blow, and the hosts took advantage to turn the win into a rout. Schlotterbeck, with a header, Wirtz, with another stunning goal, and Gruda gave the match its final numbers.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a statement published on Friday, the Court of Arbitration for Sport(CAS) mentioned it had overturned International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) decisions, which exclude Russia from events during the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships.
  • In the statement, the CAS cited a lack of sufficient evidence to support security concerns cited by the IIHF in its decisions to exclude Russian teams from competition.
  • Specifically, it ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in five upcoming tournaments, including the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany next May and the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship scheduled for November 2027 in Canada.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a statement published on Friday, the Court of Arbitration for Sport(CAS) mentioned it had overturned International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) decisions, which exclude Russia from events during the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships.

In the statement, the CAS cited a lack of sufficient evidence to support security concerns cited by the IIHF in its decisions to exclude Russian teams from competition.

Specifically, it ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in five upcoming tournaments, including the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany next May and the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship scheduled for November 2027 in Canada.

The first tournament affected by the ruling is the Men's World Junior Championship, which opens in Edmonton on December 26. The Women's World Championship being hosted by Denmark starting next Friday, November 6, is not mentioned in the statement.

Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyaryov hailed the CAS ruling, writing on the Telegram social media app that CAS had "recognized the demands of the Russian Hockey Federation on key points as justified.".

The IIHF expressed disappointment with the ruling , saying it "maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions.".

"While the IIHF respects the authority of CAS and will act in accordance with its ruling, the outcome does not remove the concerns that informed its assessments.".

Germany's ice hockey association, the DEB, also expressed disappointment at the decision.

"Our position is unchanged: We reject the return of Russian national teams to international ice hockey tournaments," stated DEB chairman Frank Lutz, who added that the ruling had fundamentally changed things for Germany as hosts of the 2027 Men's World Championship.

It has been revealed that "Allowing Russia to participate entails significant security-related, political, and economic consequences for us as hosts. We are now evaluating the ruling together with the IIHF and will provide information regarding the next steps.".

In its statement, the IIHF also pointed to "significant practical implications for competitions already at an advanced stage of preparation," which includes the men's tournament to be hosted by Düsseldorf, Mannheim and Gelsenkirchen and for which the groups have already been drawn.

Recent findings suggest that among the teams slated to participate in the tournament are Ukraine, who are set to make their return to ice hockey's international top flight after winning promotion at this year's Division 1 tournament in Poland. Ukraine had spent two decades in international ice hockey's second tier since being relegated in 2007.

Unsurprisingly, the Ukranian federation (FHU) has also condemned the CAS decision.

In a recent development, "The Ice Hockey Federation of Ukraine respects the authority and status of the CAS. At the same time, we express our deep indignation at this decision, made amidst a full-scale war," it said in a statement.

"The threats that served as the basis for the suspension of Russian teams in 2022 have not disappeared; on the contrary, they have only intensified.".

The IIHF has barred Russian teams from its tournaments since shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. This meant Russia also missed this year's prestigious Olympic hockey tournaments in Milan earlier this year.

Russia and its predecessor, the Soviet Union, are one of the most successful ice hockey-playing nations, having won 27 men's World Championships, second only to Canada (28).

Friday's ruling comes with the IIHF having just elected a upcoming president – Germany's Franz Reindl took over from Luc Tardif of France earlier this month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026.

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'.

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino noted when his contract was signed.

According to recent reports, yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

It has been revealed that so now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

In a recent development, but Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United.

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm.

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England.

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

According to recent reports, but he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

Sources indicate that the results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

All the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have noted in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

But it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results.

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success.

In a recent development, the Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

Recent findings suggest that middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'.

Industry observers note that but not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling.

In a recent development, all of this being stated, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

Now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

Industry observers note that it never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (418 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 17 Nov 2026 07:18, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 07:24.

Germany continued their impressive progress under former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp with a commanding 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday evening, with Florian Wirtz producing a standout performance.

The Reds midfielder scored twice in his 50th international appearance, including a spectacular left-footed effort, as Germany recorded their biggest victory over their neighbours since 1959.

Wirtz's display earned widespread praise in his homeland, with several publications awarding him the highest possible grade on the German school-style marking system, where 1 is the best, and 6 is the worst.

SPORT1 awarded Wirtz 1/6, describing his performance as "Ein magischer Abend des Hoffnungsträgers" - a 'magical' evening from the team's star of hope.

The publication acknowledged that he initially struggled to influence proceedings but praised his response after the interval, highlighting his spectacular first goal, subsequent brace-completing finish and ability to dictate Germany's attacking play. Sport Bild also hailed the Liverpool star's 'magic' on an impressive night.

FOCUS Online and Eurosport Germany also awarded Wirtz 1/6, with the latter describing him as the "überragende Mann" - the 'outstanding' player - after his two goals and impressive work out of possession.

FOCUS were particularly impressed by his response to an imperfect moment, joking that he had once dribbled the ball out of play unchallenged before showing his true quality with a "superb brace".

The Frankfurter Rundschau also handed him 1/6, describing him as the "Dreh- und Angelpunkt im Offensivspiel" - the 'focal point' of Germany's attacking play - while suggesting Klopp's system was allowing him to flourish.

Industry observers note that märkische Oderzeitung were slightly less generous, awarding Wirtz 1.5/6, but still praised his technical quality and two excellent finishes. They noted that he initially struggled to find decisive openings before becoming increasingly influential after the hour mark.

Sportschau did not provide a rating but similarly acknowledged that Wirtz was relatively subdued during the first half, before writing that he "Krönte seinen immer stärkeren Auftritt dann mit zwei Treffern" - capped his 'increasingly influential performance' with two goals.

The German media's enthusiasm inevitably raises the question of whether Wirtz can reproduce his international form more consistently at Anfield heading into a busy festive period.

There is little doubt that the 23-year-old has shown encouraging signs during his second season at Liverpool, registering two goals and five assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. However, these returns are still considerably below the extraordinary numbers he produced during his time at Bayer Leverkusen.

Wirtz registered 35 goals and 44 assists in 140 Bundesliga appearances for Leverkusen, becoming one of Europe's most exciting attacking midfielders. While adapting to English football and the Reds' demands takes time, he has yet to consistently reach those same creative and goalscoring heights for his club.

There have been encouraging developments, including scoring and assisting in their 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on November 8th, but the German's international performances are increasingly setting the benchmark for what supporters will expect.

His next opportunity to demonstrate that improvement comes in a huge Premier League encounter, with Liverpool welcoming Manchester United to Anfield on Sunday 22nd November.

After producing two goals against the Netherlands and earning a near-unanimous collection of top marks in Germany, Wirtz will return to Merseyside with considerable confidence. Klopp's influence on the national team has also provided an encouraging reminder of the football that Wirtz can produce when operating with freedom and confidence.

Liverpool will hope that his international brilliance can become a more regular feature at club level, particularly with one of their biggest fixtures of the season approaching.

Mikael Silvestre sees Estevao as a player capable of strengthening Manchester United, but does not believe the Red Devils will pursue the forward at this time.

According to recent reports, the former France defender, who played for the Old Trafford club between 1999 and 2008, praised the Brazilian’s performance and considered him an interesting option if he were available on the market. However, that prospect hinges on the young player’s willingness to fight for his place at Stamford Bridge.

In a recent development, silvestre’s assessment comes at a time of significant change at Manchester United. The club invested more than £144m (€170m) in signings last summer and showed an intention to back Michael Carrick after the team finished last season in third place in the Premier League. The start of the latest campaign, however, has fallen short of expectations.

In a recent development, the enthusiasm that had arisen among the fans was quickly replaced by dissatisfaction with the results. After the 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea, Manchester United reached nine consecutive matches without a win in all competitions. Neither the reaction against Roma, with a comeback in the Europa League, nor the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford was enough to prevent the departure of Carrick, who was sacked last Thursday (12 November).

In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino has been chosen to take charge of the team. The Argentinian has officially left the United States national team and is expected to begin work at Manchester United this week, while the board is already focusing its attention on the January transfer window.

Among the possibilities to strengthen the squad, Estevao appears as a name that appeals to Silvestre. The 19-year-old Brazilian is still seeking greater playing time at Chelsea, but he had a standout performance precisely against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge.

In an interview with Betarades.gr, the former player highlighted the forward’s display and pointed to his determination as an obstacle to a possible transfer.

Industry observers note that ‘Estevao played for Chelsea against Manchester United, and I think he showed why he deserves more playing time. It looks like he is going to fight for his place, so I do not think Manchester United will make a move for him’ - Silvestre mentioned.

The Frenchman’s interpretation is that the Brazilian intends to seize opportunities to establish himself at Chelsea rather than seek a move at this time. Even so, Silvestre left no doubt about his individual assessment of the player.

‘But he is definitely a good player. He plays for the Brazil national team, and I like his style of play. If he were available for transfer, he would be a good signing for Manchester United’ - he added.

Manchester United are set to return to the transfer market in January with the intention of improving the team’s performance in the second half of the season. One of their priorities is signing a left-back, a position for which the club unsuccessfully attempted to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle in the summer.

In a recent development, the attacking department may also receive attention from the board. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, considered key players for the team, have had starts to the season below expectations, increasing the need to find alternatives in attack.

With Pochettino about to begin his tenure, planning for the next transfer window is gaining importance. Estevao, despite having Silvestre’s approval, would depend on a change of scenery at Chelsea to effectively enter Manchester United’s radar.

For now, the most likely scenario is that the Brazilian will remain in London trying to gain more playing time and consolidate his position at Chelsea.

Manchester United were strongly linked with a move for Hall during the summer market but were ultimately unable to get a deal over the line for the England international.

The left-back then signed a upcoming deal with Newcastle until the summer of 2031.

The 22-year-old's future remain the subject of much speculation, with Man United still believed to be keen to bring the Englishman to Old Trafford.

Man United have struggled at left-back this season due to Luke Shaw's injury problems, while Patrick Dorgu has also only just returned from a hamstring problem.

The Red Devils will bring a latest left-back to Old Trafford in 2027, and it is clear that Hall is their number one target in that area of the field given his age and quality.

Signing Hall off the back of a new deal at Newcastle will be far from straightforward, but Man United must push to bring the Englishman to Old Trafford next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bundesliga champions Bayern Munich are to travel to Nairobi, Kenya during the winter break to play a friendly that opens the newly finished Raila Odinga International Stadium in the capital city. The German side will face Ajax Amsterdam as the game acts as part of the country's preparations for the 2027 African Cup of Nations (AFCON), which will be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania next summer.

"Bayern has millions of fantastic fans in Africa with whom we feel a close connection – it's a continent with a huge passion for football," Rouven Kasper, Bayern board member for marketing and sales, said in a club statement.

"We will be making a further contribution to raising the profile of the Bundesliga and are very much looking forward to this special event.".

The news is just the latest venture into global sports investing in Africa. Earlier this month, Formula 1 declared it was returning to the continent after Rwanda secured the rights for a deal from the early 2030s onwards. In September, World Athletics revealed Nairobi would host the World Championships in 2029. It will be the first time the event has been held in Africa.

Simon Chadwick, a business management and program director at the African School of Economics, believes that over the last two decades the professionalization and industrialization of sports has begun to emerge in Africa.

"Countries like Rwanda, Kenya, Morocco and obviously, South Africa, if we go back to the last decade of the previous century, have increasingly begun to deploy sport as a policy instrument," Chadwick told DW, adding Senegal and Egypt to the list.

Industry observers note that "There are these image and reputational benefits which very often are bundled up as soft power. It's about attractiveness and appeal and engagement," remarked Chadwick.

"It's almost like a kind of professionalization, industrialization and politicization of sport that we're seeing elsewhere in the world has now arrived in Africa. We are seeing a much greater sense of kind of self-determination within Africa to do this," he added.

Recent findings suggest that "This is not just about sport. It is also about diplomacy and bilateral trade, but also about the broader economic and industrial context within which sport sits.".

Recent findings suggest that for Kenya specifically, the building of the stadium is in line with the housing and sports infrastructural development that has been so heavily promoted under President William Ruto. Hosting this game is a symbol of the development right now happening in Nairobi.

"The bigger picture is that Nairobi now is positioning itself as a as an alternative sports venue," Richard Wanjohi, Editorial and Research Lead at the African Sports and Creative Institute (ASCI), told DW.

Industry observers note that "I think we have seen what Kigali has done over the last number of years. For us to then come back into this conversation as a major city that can host such an event, it's huge. A few weeks later, we'll have the rugby sevens series again and then ultimately, the Africa Cup of Nations in July.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Chadwick believes that unlike Rwanda, Kenya's relative stability and pre-existing tourist industry allows for a more natural development of sports investment.

Sources indicate that "This is not Kenya trying to build a tourism industry through an engagement in sport. I think it's an extension of what Kenya has been doing for a number of years through sport.".

Combined with being a multi-sport country - athletics, rugby, football, volleyball – Wanjohi believes Kenya is ready to make the most of that performance on the field or track.

"It's about time that we also host the world and show them that we can do this from a hosting perspective, but also from developing infrastructure that is ready to host such sports events," Wanjohi said.

"It's beyond just saying that we have the talent that is already in the sport, but it's saying that we have the infrastructure, we have the skills, we have the capability to host this as any other African, if not global nation.".

Industry observers note that however, Ruto's government has been criticized over taxation, unemployment and its handling of dissent. Given that this stadium cost approximately €375 million ($418 million), it is perhaps no surprise that questions are being asked about the decision to invest in major sports infrastructure.

Sources indicate that "People are asking, we are a struggling economy. There are a lot of other complications that could be addressed, like the education sector, health and all that. How did we get that money and be able to make that provision? Also interestingly, is that there's an appearance fee that is going to be paid to both Bayern and Ajax," said Wanjohi, who added there was also some frustration that the opening game was not given to local teams or even the national side.

Ultimately, the timing of this also matters. While many sports fans in the country are excited, others are critical.

Recent findings suggest that "The government knows that this is almost like a campaign tool. We have an election coming up in August next year so the government or the president of the day obviously wants to use as much leverage of such an event to milk it for all it's worth," Wanjohi added.

"So the two different schools of thought are: It's a good thing to have, but at what cost are we doing it at and is it in the public interest as well?".

The proof will be in what the legacy of events like Bayern Munich's friendly in Nairobi brings Kenyan football. The feeling in late 2026 though, is largely optimistic.

"I guess the acid test is that many African nations carry with them the baggage from the past that this is just trophy asset investment that is ultimately going to create white, white elephant infrastructure," Chadwick said.

"But having spoken to people in Kenyan sport, in the industry itself, it seems to me that there is a genuine appetite for sports to become a genuine and legitimate driver of economic activity.".

Janek Speight contributed reporting for this article.

Rice is aware of what Souness has said but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ stated Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’.

Rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’.

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

It has been revealed that ‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

Sources indicate that ‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’.

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died.

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch.

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'.

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

According to recent reports, owono stated: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono stated he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono).

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono.

Real Madrid are reportedly interested in signing Brighton & Hove Albion duo Luka Vuskovic and Chema Andres.

Brighton have been outstanding this season, especially in England's top flight, with the Seagulls right now sitting second in the Premier League table behind the champions Arsenal.

A record of seven wins, one draw and two defeats has seen the Seagulls pick up 22 points, while they are the leading goalscorers in the Premier League this term with 26.

Seven goals conceded represents the second-best defensive record, meanwhile, and Vuskovic has been a standout performer following his arrival from Tottenham Hotspur.

The 19-year-old has scored once and provided two assists in 16 appearances for Brighton this term, and his performances have already led to a host of attention.

Real Madrid are in the market for another centre-back, and according to TEAMtalk, the Spanish giants are huge admirers of Vuskovic.

The Croatia international has a contract at the Amex until the summer of 2031, with the option of a further year, placing Brighton in a strong position.

However, the Seagulls will find it difficult to keep hold of him on a long-term basis if the likes of Real Madrid begin a serious pursuit of the teenager.

Real Madrid are also allegedly keeping a close eye on the performances of their former player Andres, who moved to Brighton from Stuttgart over the summer.

The 21-year-old has one goal and one assist in nine appearances for Brighton this term.

Andres, who is a 6ft 4in defensive midfielder, played for Real Madrid between 2018 and 2025, progressing through the youth system to the first team.

The Spaniard played three times for Real Madrid's senior team during the 2024-25 campaign before moving to Stuttgart, featuring on 41 occasions for the German club ahead of a move to the Premier League.

There have previously been claims that Los Blancos have some form of buyback option on Andres, but Brighton are allegedly confident that is not the case.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.

North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

A glass cabinet containing memorabilia linked to the 1958 Munich Air Disaster, in which eight Manchester United footballers lost their lives, was smashed and plundered in the Munich suburb of Trudering this week.

The display case on Manchesterplatz forms part of a memorial commemorating the tragedy which occurred when the United team made a refueling stop in Munich while on the way back from a European Cup game in Belgrade, Serbia, on February 6, 1958.

Recent findings suggest that the plane struggled to take off again in the wintery conditions at the old Munich-Riem airport to the east of the city center and, on the third attempt, ploughed off the end of the runway and into a house. Of the 44 people on board, 23 were killed, including eight United players, several journalists and two crew members.

The crash site has become a place of pilgrimage for United supporters and, in 2020, the cabinet was installed on the initiative of the Red Docs Munich – a local Bayern Munich fan club – to house the various memorabilia and tributes left by visitors.

According to recent reports, munich police stated the cabinet was broken into on Monday morning between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (07:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. UTC), with the unknown perpetrators making off with a glass sculpture and several medals.

The Red Docs Munich arranged for replacement glass to be installed on the same day. The MMMF noted Manchester United had offered to pay for the repairs but said the foundation had covered the costs itself.

A ban on upcoming Stolpersteine ("stumbling stones") to commemorate victims of the Holocaust in the eastern German town of Heidenau will be upheld after five petitions against the measure were thrown out.

Local councilors from Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) voted together in September to pass the controversial ban on new stones being laid in the town in Saxony, near Dresden.

Petitions against the measure were submitted from across Germany — as well as one from the Netherlands — calling for victims of the Nazi regime to continue to be remembered in Heidenau by way of the small metal plaques embedded in pavements.

During his final day of a whirlwind Asia tour this week, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul on Friday that Germany and Europe are ready to cooperate with Asian economies to foster a rules-based economic order.

Merz stated the European Union is ready to take the lead in shaping a better deal for countries in Asia feeling the pressure of a destabilized rules-based trade order.

"Competition between the US and China is ramping up. Tariffs, technological decoupling strategies and a tough race for critical raw materials and new technologies are fundamentally changing the rules of our global economy," Merz said.

"There is a fear that we might be facing ‌a new wave of European protectionism - that we are closing ‌ourselves off from other nations," ‌Merz said.

Citing Germany as an example, South Korean Prime Minister Han Seong Sook told the conference  "German companies are using Korea as a central hub to expand their presence in the Asia-Pacific region.".

Liverpool's bigger problemShape. Liverpool’s shape is a sight to behold and one that you can see quite clearly anytime you watch them: because it doesn’t really change. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Jurgen Klopp is in dreamland after witnessing a “truly extraordinary” performance from his Germany side in a statement 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.
  • The four-time world champions began the night sitting third in League A Group 2 and knew that they had to claim maximum points against the Oranje at the summit to secure top spot and qualify for the quarter-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 09:46.

Jurgen Klopp is in dreamland after witnessing a “truly extraordinary” performance from his Germany side in a statement 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

The four-time world champions began the night sitting third in League A Group 2 and knew that they had to claim maximum points against the Oranje at the summit to secure top spot and qualify for the quarter-finals.

With so much at stake heading into the sixth and final matchday, Die Mannschaft rose to the occasion in prolific fashion, claiming their biggest win against their Dutch neighbours since 1959 when they won 7-0.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring just before half time with a sensational maiden international goal, setting the tone for a dominant second-half display.

Overwhelmed by Germany’s relentless high press, the Netherlands had no answer as two goals from Florian Wirtz, and strikes from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda, sealed a statement triumph for Klopp’s side.

It has been revealed that “What we’ve just witnessed was truly extraordinary,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters post-match. “The game was extraordinary, and incredibly difficult.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way to win. We had to adapt and make a few adjustments, some fairly significant ones, but we made them. We took away a lot of their strengths, and then we scored some incredible goals. That was unbelievable.

“It was a fantastic football match and a wonderful experience. I wouldn’t have ever dreamed of having the chance to do this in Berlin in front of a sold-out crowd. In the final international game of the year, it’s amazing.”.

In addition to progressing to the quarter-finals, the result served as compelling evidence of Germany's renaissance and progress under Klopp, with his arrival fostering renewed optimism around his youthful squad.

Germany failed to win their opening two Nations League matches, but they ended their group campaign with 11 points (W3 D2 L1) and have conceded a competition-low three goals in six games.

Recent findings suggest that "The moment I arrived here, I fell in love with this team at first sight,” noted Klopp. “I'm at the beginning of this journey.

Recent findings suggest that “I simply feel that we have a fantastic football team and a very good footballing idea that can work extremely well. If we can get these highly-talented players firing, then we're going to be a very difficult team to play against.

“We scored some incredible goals and, with increasing confidence, put in a great performance in front of a fantastic crowd. It’s been a lot of fun to work with this team, and we feel like we have a very special group of players here.

“But this is still only just the beginning – after six games, we can’t say that we’ve arrived where we want to be yet, as there are still lots of things we can improve on.”.

Recent findings suggest that "Everyone who was here today is going home with a smile, and won't be questioning the German national team for the next three or four months. That's a good thing," Klopp added when referring to the negativity that lingered previously around the national team.

Looking ahead to the quarter-final draw on Friday, Klopp added: "The lads can head home now with a smile on their faces as the group winners. We’ll watch the draw later this week and wait and see what sort of crunch match we’ll get, as there are only strong teams left.”.

Germany, who have risen to 11th in the FIFA World Rankings, will play their two-legged quarter-final tie in March 2027, with a first-placed finish in League A rewarded with a second leg on home soil.

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.

Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.

In five matches to date in the Nations League, the manager has not yet been able to select the same back-three in two consecutive outings. Injuries and suspensions have seen to that.

For all that, you sense that even if he’d had a full quota of players to choose from, Pocognoli would still be figuring out his preferred defensive grouping.

This does feel like a time of opportunity for those who are fresh on the scene. Catch the eye and there’s a real chance to become established as a mainstay of the team moving forward.

Luke Graham did his chances of doing just that no harm at all in his first start and second cap for his country on Friday.

Playing in between Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney, the Stoke City man made a compelling case to stay there with a strong and diligent display.

Luke Graham enjoyed a composed debut for Scotland as they recorded a much-needed win.

On the back of a summer move from Dundee to the English Championship, Graham appears to have taken the step-up to international level in his stride.

‘It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up, so I have to be ready for the moment and take it when it comes,’ he said.

‘I think there’s good competition. We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously, it was unfortunate for Welshy (Stephen Welsh) and Binksy (Luis Binks) to go out with injury, but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place.

Sources indicate that ‘When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens going forward.’.

Timing can be vital in football. And it’s conceivable that Graham’s might just propel him to become a Scotland regular.

While playing at Dens Park saw him mentioned in dispatches with regards to a call-up, his move to England, coming just before Pocognoli was declared as Steve Clarke’s successor, has seen his dream quickly become reality.

‘I’ve always noted that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special,’ he reflected.

Former Dundee defender Graham proudly belts out the national anthem ahead of kick-off.

‘Not much is going wrong for me at the moment, so it’s just about maintaining that and keeping it going every week.

Sources indicate that ‘I wouldn’t say I merited a start as we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He just remarked to go out and enjoy it and do what you’re doing every week at Stoke. I think I did all right.’.

Notwithstanding how limited the North Macedonians were on the night, Pocognoli was entitled to take encouragement from the way the back three acquitted themselves.

Industry observers note that playing closer to each other than we’d seen in the previous matches, they were rarely unpicked by balls through the middle. Angus Gunn was not overworked in goal. Tellingly, the only concession of the night came when Scott McTominay lost his man at a corner.

‘I think a lot of it is just being brave,’ Graham reflected. ‘It’s about bravery in going man-to-man with the striker, being brave on the ball, trying to break the lines and keeping possession.

‘So, I think bravery is the main thing and concentration as well.’.

Graham keeps a close eye on North Macedonian danger man Elmin Rastoder at Hampden.

In a recent development, with the defence solid enough, Pocognoli had a platform for a much-needed win. While the narrow scoreline made the final moments more anxious than they should have been, on balance, Scotland were deserved winners.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s just about winning games at this stage of the competition, so that was good,’ mentioned Graham. ‘I think, if I’m being harsh, we should have killed the game off before it got to 1-1. We had a few good chances to put them to bed.

‘Then we kinda shot ourselves in the foot by conceding from a set piece. But Ben Gannon-Doak does well for the penalty and for us to go 2-1 up and see it out was good.’.

No one would dispute that the display was a long way from perfect. There’s significant room for improvement ahead of the concluding group match with Switzerland on Monday.

‘We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go,’ Graham said. ‘It’s about adjusting and trying to build on performances in every game. I think it’s going to take time.

‘It’s a different style, a different manager and we just have to keep being patient. You look at the squad now and there’s a lot of newly introduced, young players coming through. It’s just about encouraging us young boys and showing we can get a place in the squad.

‘It is going to take time but, once we get there, we’re going to do really well and compete right at the top of the game.’.

Graham has been a huge success in Stoke's flying start to the Championship season.

Graham does look like he’s moving in the right direction. From watching Scotland compete at the World Cup on licensed premises five months ago, he hopes he too can be the toast of the nation one day.

‘I didn’t go. It was too expensive for me,’ he explained. ‘I think I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day.

‘I wasn’t too far away (previously), I think. Steve Clarke, the former manager, told me that. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully getting there one day.

Industry observers note that ‘There’s been a lot of hard work and dedication which has led me to this point. I’m very grateful to a lot of people who have helped me in my career so far and just to get this chance is amazing.’.

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 09:54.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United have reportedly identified Lille defender Nathan Ngoy as a potential transfer target.

Unai Emery's and Matthias Jaissle's sides went into the November international break sitting in 10th and 12th place respectively in the Premier League table.

Not only will both managers be disappointed with those positions, there will be concern that with their respective defensive records.

Villa have conceded 17 goals from their 10 top-flight fixtures in 2026-27, while the Magpies have shipped one goal fewer.

Therefore, strengthening in that area of the pitch has become a priority for the two managers ahead of 2027.

According to MilanNews24, Villa and Newcastle are 'making strong moves' to sign Belgium international Ngoy.

In sharp contrast to the two Premier League clubs, Lille have only conceded seven goals in 10 Ligue 1 fixtures, with Ngoy featuring in nine of those matches.

The 23-year-old has promptly become an established figure for his country, starting all six of their recent UEFA Nations League matches and scoring in the 4-1 win over Italy on Sunday.

While he possesses a contract at Lille until 2029, it remains to be seen whether Lille would be able to reject any substantial offers for his signature.

AC Milan have also been credited as admirers of the former Standard Liege player, who can deputise at right-back when required.

Although Villa signed Taylor Harwood-Bellis during the summer, he has not been viewed as a like-for-like replacement for Ezri Konsa.

Instead, Emery has been relying on three centre-backs in Victor Lindelof, Pau Torres and Tyrone Mings who are all aged between 29 and 33, essentially ensuring that alternatives will eventually need to be found.

Newcastle are in a similar position, with Fabian Schar and Dan Burn both aged 34 and right-back Tino Livramento having suffered regular injuries.

In both cases, Ngoy could become a first-team player should he move to Villa Park or St James' Park next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have so much work to do on their first-team squad.

The Anfield outfit have been left in the dust by their title rivals with Arsenal now nine points clear of them in the Premier League.

Indeed, the fact that the Reds are fourth in the table is good news as, it means that they're still in the running for the Champions League.

However, after Arne Slot was sacked for finishing fifth last season, you'd have thought that the Anfield outfit would be trying to do much better than they did then, especially if they want to keep Andoni Iraola as their boss.

Obviously, transfers can help with this and now, the Reds have been told exactly how much they'll have to bid if they want to sign one of their latest transfer targets.

Galatasaray want to bump Aleksey Batrakov's release clause up to €100m.

Liverpool have been lacking a creative spark among their ranks for a while now.

When Trent Alexander-Arnold was still around, he was their main source of chances.

However, since he chose to leave Anfield for the Bernabeu a couple of years ago, the Reds have been trying to fill the void he left behind.

That obviously hasn't worked out all that well, even with the £116 million purchase of Florian Wirtz.

Since then, many different players have been linked with Liverpool and, one of the more recent and intriguing options has been Aleksey Batrakov.

The Russian at the moment plays for Galatasaray in the Turkish Super Lig and, so far this season he's bagged six goals for the club with four of them coming in the Champions League.

This form hasn't gone unnoticed with Turkish outlet Takvim now sharing how much Galatasaray seem to want for their 21-year-old star.

"Following interest from European clubs in the transfer, Galatasaray management is reportedly preparing to amend Batrakov's contract," they wrote.

"Galatasaray is planning to meet with the player's agent in the coming days.

"The Russian footballer, who has a contract with Galatasaray until 2031, has a €55 million release clause in his current contract.

"The management aims to increase this figure to 100 million euros with the newly introduced agreement.".

Aleksey Batrakov could be exactly what Liverpool need.

From the 13 games that Batrakov has played for Galatasaray this season, he's swiftly become one of their best players.

During those games, he's contributed to 10 goals across all competitions and has been used as a number 10 and a number eight.

His performances in both positions have been impeccable but, it's on the attack where he really shines.

Batrakov's ability to create a chance out of nothing and even get in on the goals himself is exactly what Liverpool are missing at the moment.

Obviously, nothing is set in stone yet and if Galatasaray do bump his release clause up to €100 million from €55 million, there's probably no chance of the Reds bringing him in any time soon.

But, for now, it's nice to know that Julian Ward and Iraola are keeping their eyes open for any possible deals that could benefit Liverpool.

#25542. Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

"People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

It has been revealed that "A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

Industry observers note that but a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, reveals how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

According to recent reports, names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer stated their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

According to recent reports, research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

"Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

Even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

According to recent reports, pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

Recent findings suggest that "People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

Later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she remarked.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Sources indicate that tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

But the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

Sources indicate that "I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

In a recent development, but Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum stated.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

In a recent development, that does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

Industry observers note that pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

Published: 17:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has backed Ben Gannon-Doak to find his killer instinct in the final third and establish himself as Scotland’s main man.

The Bournemouth youngster had an up-and-down evening in Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win over North Macedonia, getting into numerous promising positions on the right flank and winning the penalty – dispatched by John McGinn – which decided the game.

But, as has been the case throughout his Scotland career, the 21-year-old’s final ball in key moments left a lot to be desired.

Pocognoli is under no illusions that Gannon-Doak still has plenty to improve on, but insists that it won’t be long before things start to click for the talented youngster.

‘As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one v ones I am happy,’ said the Belgian. ‘With Ben, we know that he is at a young age and needs to work on specific things.

‘On Friday, he had great opportunities. We know that he needs to improve on the end product, but he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets Ben Gannon-Doak as he is substituted at Hampden.

Industry observers note that ‘He did that last night as well. We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball. I am happy with his performance.

According to recent reports, ‘He is a young lad, just 21. Okay, he has become more mature than he was, but I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making.

It has been revealed that ‘I believe if he is playing every game he can make many decisions. He will know that in the next game he will have to do it again.

‘If he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks, sometimes he can think, “This is my moment”.

‘It is a process. He will become older and at some point will become relaxed in his decision making, but at this very young age what he is producing is very good.

Sources indicate that ‘I say exactly the same thing to him after training on the pitch. I say, “Ben, this is the next step”. He knows that and it is key he knows that.’.

Scotland conclude their Nations League campaign in Switzerland on Monday knowing that only a victory against the group winners will be enough if they are to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia – currently one point better off ahead of their trip to North Macedonia – into second spot.

Pocognoli admits Gannon-Doak's end product has to improve after another frustrating show.

Should that happen, Scotland would have a crack at earning promotion to League A via a play-off in March, and also crucially guarantee their place as a Pot 2 side for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

‘We are still alive in this competition,’ said Pocognoli, who celebrated his first win at Hampden on Friday at the third time of asking. ‘We know we have to do more than this competition. This competition is about trying to build something.

‘But it is nice to have that possibility on Monday to try to create something against one of the top 20 teams in the world.

‘We need to try to be brave. Switzerland have already qualified so let’s go there and be smart because they are a good team.

According to recent reports, ‘It is part of the process to play away against a top team. That is not something we have done yet. The approach will be different and, for me as a coach, it is a game with a lot of responsibility.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 11:04.

Outgoing USA manager Mauricio Pochettino has publicly advised Pep Guardiola to pursue the vacant national team job as he prepares to begin his new role at Manchester United.

The 54-year-old Argentine will bid an emotional farewell to the Stars and Stripes when he takes charge of his final fixture against Haiti on Tuesday before officially taking over from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

With the US Soccer Federation now searching for a successor, former Manchester City boss Guardiola has emerged as a ‘top target’ for the vacant managerial role.

Addressing the media during his final pre-match press conference, Pochettino gave his endorsement to the legendary Catalan coach - who won 20 trophies across 10 seasons at Man City - and urged him to accept an offer if approached.

"Take it," Pochettino told reporters. "Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation.

“Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it. Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style.".

While Pochettino is backing Guardiola for international management, a previous conversation between the pair helped trigger the Argentine's own return to the club game.

Last week, Man United confirmed Pochettino as their new head coach after dismissing Carrick, who has left the Red Devils languishing in the Premier League relegation zone following a dismal start to the campaign.

Taking the reins at Carrington marks Pochettino's first club appointment since departing Chelsea at the conclusion of the 2023-24 season, adding to previous English top-flight stints with Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Pochettino was given the green light by Man United to see out his USA commitments first, with his final outing against Haiti largely a formality after the Stars and Stripes secured a dominant 6-0 win in the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday.

In an interview with The Telegraph ahead of his departure, Pochettino disclosed that he confessed to Guardiola how much he longed for the daily routine of club football when the pair met at an MLS game between Upcoming York Red Bulls and New York City FC in September.

According to recent reports, “I am ready [to return],” Pochettino explained. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’.

“[He remarked] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

It has been revealed that “But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything… this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”.

Pochettino’s candid remarks about craving a Premier League comeback may frustrate some USA supporters, given that he had put pen to paper on a new four-year contract extension just one month before his discussion with Guardiola.

One of the best ways for the Reds to combat this is to sign fresh players to plug the gaps their current squad are leaving open.

Obviously, some positions are more of a problem than others with Liverpool likely to have a priority position that they want to strengthen.

But, if they manage to cover all the potential positions they need to, they'll have a massive selection of players to choose from which would obviously be beneficial for them.

Since the Reds aren't a club who have an endless amount of money to spend, their transfers need to mean something which is why their next big deal is hinging on a major decision from the Anfield outfit.

Liverpool are unlikely to sign Lamine Camara in January.

Lamine Camara was one of the main players linked with a Liverpool transfer in the summer.

It was clear to almost everyone that a latest midfielder was one of the main things that Iraola needed to take the Reds to the next level.

Obviously, replacing Mohamed Salah was also one of the main things that they needed to do but, with how much players such as Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have struggled to adapt to Iraola's system, the Reds have managed to dig themselves into a bit of a hole.

Because, even though they were desperate for a new midfielder in the summer, by January, it'll be more than clear to every team in the world that a new midfielder is required by the Reds.

In the summer, Camara was available for a cut-rate deal and now, he's worth around €70 million.

The fact of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch also having prominent roles among their ranks also needs to be taken into consideration as, if another midfielder is brought in, the minutes played by each player will diminish.

And, according to David Lynch via Anfield Index, this could be the thing to stop them from signing the Senegal international.

"I know the reports, but still struggle to see Lamine Camara to Liverpool in January without a significant departure," he noted.

"Endo doesn’t play at all, more a Gravenberch or Szoboszlai which it’s hard to see, otherwise there’s a question of minutes. Liverpool don’t like to be over stocked as we know.".

Lamine Camara would be a perfect transfer for Liverpool.

Before the summer, Camara was probably a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of.

The midfielder was quietly making a name for himself in Ligue 1 and then, when Filipe Luis took over as their manager, he instantly became one of the first names on their team sheet.

From that point on, clubs from across the world were interested in the midfielder and have remained so ever since.

But, of all the teams he's been linked with, Liverpool are the team he'd be perfect for.

Not only would he perfectly fit into Iraola's prepares but, he'd also be able to come in for one of his starting midfielders.

Indeed, the €70 million fee is a bit of a risk but, in reality, that's the going rate for a decent central midfielder these days.

Here's hoping that Liverpool come to their senses and get a deal over the line.
